title: Demand Response Programs Rules on Calling Events and Recording Participation
content:
## Program rules — events and participation (Demand Response Programs)

**Rule 1 — When events may be called.** Events are called only within the program's event season, on its event days and inside its event window, with the program's advance notice hours of notice through its event notification channels, and never beyond the program's most events per season, most event hours per season or longest single event.

**Rule 2 — Recording an event.** Each event is recorded once per enrollment, with the baseline under the program's baseline method. Participation is recorded only for an enrollment in active status.

**Rule 3 — Opt-outs.** Where the program allows opt-outs, the customer may opt out of an event, and opt-outs beyond the program's opt-outs per season carry the program's consequence for excess opt-outs.

**Rule 4 — Device limits in an event.** Battery dispatch never draws the battery below the program's battery reserve share, thermostat events never move the setpoint more than the program's largest setpoint change, and cycling events switch the compressor off for the program's cycling share of each half-hour.

## How the season counts are taken

- **Events and event hours in the season** — the events recorded on the enrollment within the current event season (the event season of the program year that contains the date the question is handled), counted, together with the total of their event hours. These counts are measured against the program's most events and most event hours per season.
- **Opt-outs in the season** — the events recorded on the enrollment within the current event season in which the customer opted out, counted. This count is measured against the program's opt-outs per season.

## What each event record carries

One record per event per enrollment, identified by the company's event code, showing: the date of the event; whether it was a test event; whether the customer opted out; the baseline usage over the event hours in kWh (0 where no baseline is computed); the metered usage over the event hours in kWh; and the average load reduction or battery discharge delivered over the event hours in kW.

## Points of judgement

| Situation | Under these rules |
|---|---|
| Enrollment in active status, event called within the program's calendar and limits | One participation record for that enrollment and event |
| Enrollment in enrolled status (not yet active) | No participation is recorded |
| Enrollment in unenrolled or removed status | No participation is recorded |
| Same event already recorded on the enrollment | Not recorded a second time |
| Customer opts out in a program that allows opt-outs | The opt-out is recorded on the event record; it counts toward the season's opt-outs |
| Opt-outs in the season pass the program's limit | The program's excess opt-out consequence applies |

## Illustration (hypothetical season)

A Smart Thermostat Rewards enrollment in active status has 9 events recorded in the current season, totalling 31 event hours, with opt-outs on 2 of them. Season counts: 9 events, 31 event hours, 2 opt-outs — within the program's 15 events, 60 event hours and 3 opt-outs.
